newsitem.title: GERMANY: Issing says against softening Maastricht Treaty.
newsitem.headline: Issing says against softening Maastricht Treaty.

text.p: Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing said on Thursday the Maastricht Treaty criteria for entry to European currency union must not be softened, and the question of political union should be addressed.

"The Maastricht convergence critieria must not be softened," Issing said in a speech at a seminar hosted by the Centre for European Reform, a British think-tank which has close links with the new left-of-centre government.
"The Maastricht Treaty is a formula that has been ratified by parliaments and it must be adhered to," he said.
Issing also said, "A Europe that is entering EMU cannot ignore the issue of political union.
He said the Maastricht Treaty is "a promise that the new common currency will deliver a new and better future for Europe".
